Serious Sam 4 is what the Doom games should have been. Thank God, Croatia has those intelligent and dedicated people working on FPSes. All of those games are pretty good. Serious Sam 2 is questionable, but at least it tried doing something different; can't fault them for that.

The Characters

But seriously, the Hell Knights have never looked like a higher fidelity version of the Doom 2 ones.

The imps have never been recognizable - not even the fucking fireballs (jeez guys, it's a fucking fireball, you can get this right) look like the ones from Doom 2. The only reason I knew the imps were the imps was because the game said it at some point, and they all kinda looked a bit different, and I just forget which creatures were the imps. They look way, way to generic. If they can't get it right they should straight up put the fucking sprite from Doom 1 & 2 in the newer games, and just quit trying, because they suck at this. Honestly, it's probably management's fault more than anything, but if the devs did fuck this up, shame on them.

The Gameplay

And what's the deal with the overwhelming number of mechanics in this game? There is a theme of "too much going on at once" to learn about how each mechanic works. Which is pushing me to look crap up online, which I wanted to avoid at all costs.

* The belch?

* The chainsaw?

* The grenade launcher (separate from the shotgun's grenade launcher)?

* The secondary and tertiary functions for each weapon (so far, there might be more, i just haven't gotten that far)

* The melee punch attack (with it's numerous different functions, that I still don't understand)

* The jump and the double jump

* The dash and the double dash

* The HUD

And each one of these things has its own nuances to them. I don't even know what the "switch equipment" control does yet nor the "crucible" function yet. How many fucking different functions do we need? Spies working at game companies who analyze data stolen from user's computers have asked why PC players are using controllers instead of mouse and keyboard. Well, I'll tell you prying sneaks why: because there are too many controls to manage on a keyboard; hell, even the controller isn't really good enough to handle all these functions. I even forgot about the weapon wheel because there was too much shit going on with the keyboard - these numerous controls do not work for the fast-pace action they're going for in this game.

The belch lasts so briefly that it clearly screams "upgrade me. do the gamey upgradey thingy". And it seems largely pointless to use, but there it is taking up a button.

The chainsaw seems tacked on in an inelegant way - you won't know if you can kill an enemy with it until you're right in their face taking damage, then it says "not enough fuel"... first of all it doesn't make sense to me that you can't at least do damage with the chainsaw, even if you can't kill a tougher demon with it - it just says "fuck you haha", and it leads you to believe that if you had more fuel you could kill it (i do not know if this is how it will eventually work). As far as I know, the game doesn't even tell you that this is how it works, you just have to take damage enough time or die to tell yourself that the weapon isn't effective. Why would an amount of fuel determine whether you can even hit a character with it, and why would anyone think that you'd only take a swing if the arbitrary condition is met that you kill the enemy with it? This mechanic is just stupid.

The grenade launcher has a janky trajectory, especially when you compare it to the other grenade launcher on the shotgun. The shotgun's works like you'd think the other one is just stupid, and almost never lands properly. I think they're trying to emulate a grenade throw, which is completely retarded since they made a gun pop out of your suit and shoot a grenade. I'm done talking about this, if you want to see how stupid this works, just look up a video.

The secondary and tertiary firing modes need to have a better way to activate the functions. They should just have a button to fire each, not a toggle, then readying button, then fire. This completely fucks up the pacing and fast-pace action they are shooting for here (which does not match a Doom game's gameplay, which I'll get to soon). The wide variety of secondary functions can get you killed so easily if you use the wrong one when switching to a weapon.

The melee punch attack gets powered up and can be used to ?do a lot of damage to things? or ?1-hit things? I'm not even sure because by the time I get to use it there's too much going on to pay attention to everything. Is the normal punch just really weak or what? I can't seem to knock out zombies with it, which are the weakest enemies in the game. This attack is also used to activate stuff, which I guess is fine, but it goes to show how overloaded the controls are.

The double jump is a welcome mechanic, I think they did this well. I like how edges are easy to grab onto. Although that amount of platforming is irritating, and not Doom-like. When they have you jumping on shit where you need to look ahead to find out what to do, or you'll fall and take damage, it pisses me off because I could be missing secrets, and they do put secrets in these areas. I've found several secrets in these areas, and if I go past an area and can't get back at some point, I'm going to be really pissed.

The double dash is fine, too. I don't like how it let's you so easily dash to the side, because that just isn't something I really want to do ever, nor do I want to have to do that on-the-fly given the way this game plays already. I like the double dash, and I think they have potential here. They should have made it work more with combat, because it looks like it's not really for use in combat so much as it is for platforming.

The HUD has way too much shit going on because of all the aforementioned mechanics, and the symbols are not intuitive. They need to do something different.

The Sound effects and music

The music is decent, but it needs to BRING THAT SHIT!!! I want to hear that guitar get fucking smashed on, and hear some riffs I've never heard before.

The cartoony sound effects when you interact with enemies is unfitting. Why does executing the Cacodemons make a cartoon stretching then popping noise? Why do some of the secrets, when activated, make children's birthday party noises? If they're trying to make a joke where they contrast the seriousness of the game with something like that they're doing it too often and too soon - it didn't work. There are a few other instances where they make cartoon effects; I'll add them when I hear them again, since I can't recall off-hand.

The "Story"

This looks like some generic ****inoffensive ****, written-by-committee crap. Why in the hell wouldn't they have drawn from a Christian view of hell as much as possible. There's all this random chatter about seemingly made-up characters and whatever else; this just leads to more incoherence with the Doom franchise. They do this every time... and it's bad; let's be clear about that. Following a Christian background would give it substance and real life relevance, and it can go way off the tracks if it wants to, but just tie that shit in there - they can even keep those giant doom slayers in the levels!!! Now, I think they're pulling some of this lore from some culture in history, but I just don't care.

The menu navigation

Not sure how or why this is a problem, but the nested menus operate intuitively. I won't be expanding this topic, because it's so stupid that this is a problem they can either fix it or have their stupidity stay there for all to see. Like those Dark Souls 1 menus (wtf btw?).
